## Performance Analysis

Note: this repo has **no React/frontend code** (0 `.tsx`/`.jsx` files) — it's a backend TypeScript agent-swarm (in-memory state, event bus, mock GCP/BigQuery clients). I looked at the closest real analogs instead: N+1-style repeated lookups in loops, "over-render"-equivalent state-broadcast overhead, unused caching infrastructure, unbounded memory growth, and redundant recomputation. Findings below are grounded in actual files/lines.

### 1. N+1-style patterns

**`src/agents/tier1/memory-agent.ts:413-452` — `consolidateMemory` is O(n²) plus per-match individual fetches**
```ts
for (const entry of allEntries) {                       // O(n)
  const similar = await this.vectorStore.search(entry.embedding, 5, threshold); // O(n) linear scan itself
  for (const s of toMerge) {
    const similarEntry = await this.vectorStore.retrieve(s.id);   // separate lookup per match
    ...
  }
}
```
`search()` already does a full linear scan per call (see #5), so this function is effectively O(n²) — for 10k memory entries that's ~100M cosine-similarity ops per consolidation pass, run on a periodic timer (`memory-agent.ts:540`). Fix: batch-retrieve matched IDs in one pass (`vectorStore.getMany(ids)`), and only run consolidation over entries changed since the last pass.

**`src/agents/tier2/risk-detection-agent.ts:207-211` — sequential await-in-loop over campaigns**
```ts
for (const campaign of campaigns) {
  const campaignAlerts = await this.analyzeSingleCampaign(campaign, context); // serialized
  ...
}
```
If `analyzeSingleCampaign` ever calls out to a real data source (BigQuery, ad platform API), this becomes classic N+1 — one round trip per campaign instead of a batched query. Fix:
```ts
const results = await Promise.all(campaigns.map(c => this.analyzeSingleCampaign(c, context)));
```

**Forward-looking**: `src/integrations/gcp/bigquery-client.ts` is currently a no-op mock. When it's wired to real BigQuery, watch every place that loops calling `.query()`
